title: RAG in 60 seconds
description: Why do chatbots make things up, and how does RAG fix it? Thoma the tech imp explains retrieval augmented generation with an open-book exam.

scenes.say: Why does a chatbot confidently make things up?
Because it answers from memory, like a student in a closed-book exam.
If it never learned the answer, it guesses. Very confidently. Like me at a quiz night.
Here's the trick. RAG gives it an open book. Your question goes to a search step, which finds the right documents.
Then the model writes the answer from those pages, not from a guess.
In code, it's basically three lines: search, add, ask.
So: RAG means look it up first, then answer. Which is why chatbots stop making things up. Thoma out!

visual.text: RAG = *look it up first*, then answer.
